White Whisper combines exploration, logic puzzles, and reading messages in a compact sci-fi narrative with a mysterious atmosphere. With the ship’s AI as your guide, you uncover traces of the crew, decipher codes, and gradually reveal the chilling secrets of the abandoned Sentinel.

Zero Gravity:

Experience zero gravity, where the concept of "up" and "down" loses all meaning. Every movement becomes a new opportunity as corridors and decks open up in unexpected directions, giving exploration a whole new dimension.

[WHO AM I] is a story-driven first-person horror game where you step into the shoes of a protagonist who has forgotten who they are and what they've done, uncovering a hideous past to confront the truth.

Synopsis 

Awakening from a recurring dream, you find yourself trapped in a repeating day. The end of each day inevitably leads to an inexplicable, agonizing nightmare. It reveals scenes that are eerily familiar, yet are things you never wanted to witness.

Is this the truth you’ve been trying to avoid? Or is it mere delusion? Face the truth that slowly unravels as the days repeat. Who are you?

Key Features

  • Escape the Dream

    Is the place you fell asleep in a dream, or reality? Search for clues within the repeating nightmares to make your escape.

  • Psychological Anomalies

    As the days repeat, reality becomes bizarrely distorted, and things that were once unseen begin to manifest.

  • Finding Clues to the Truth

    Who are you, and what exactly happened that day? Search for hidden clues scattered throughout to uncover your true identity.

Multiple Endings

Your choices lead to 3 completely different endings.

Find items hidden in the dark and choose carefully at every moment.

The decisions you make and the clues you collect will determine the final ending.

YOU'RE IN THE SAME ROOM BUT YOU DON'T SEE THE SAME THINGS!

You have to find every difference before time runs out.

Or you'll end up like the others.

How much can you trust your friends' word?

────────────────────────────

ANOMALIES

When you open the chest, the number of anomaly stones in your hand

tells you one thing: HOW MANY ANOMALIES ARE YOURS!

No two lists are the same. You'll decide together where to start.

But while you're helping the others, don't forget your own.

────────────────────────────

THE MAJORITY IS RIGHT

Three people see the arcade machine as red, one sees blue? Then

the one seeing blue is wrong.

No voting, no compromise. Just the majority — and the cold

arithmetic of being the minority.

────────────────────────────

SPECIAL STONES

Besides your anomaly seals, you might be carrying something else.

Who has what — or whether they have anything at all — no one but

you will ever know.

EYE STONE — puts a photo of whatever you're looking at on

everyone's screen for ten seconds. You show what you're trying to

describe.

SOUL STONE — reveals everyone's position for fifteen seconds. The

answer to "are we even looking at the same thing?"

ZONE STONE — opens a grid around the spot where you drop it. A

cube touching an anomaly turns green, the grid fades, the stone

stays.

It doesn't give you the answer; it tells you where to look.

One use only. Where you use it decides how much it's worth.

────────────────────────────

THE PORTAL JUDGES YOU ALONE

When time runs out, everyone must have made it back to the

starting room.

From that moment on, everyone is on their own.

Either you escape, or you live your own hell.

────────────────────────────

FEATURES

• 2-4 player online co-op — voice chat isn't a convenience, it's

the game itself

• Asymmetric perception — everyone sees a different version of the

same place

• Irreversible decisions — every seal is final, every mistake is

yours

• Special stones — show, locate, scan; who holds them stays secret

• Shared timer, individual fate — you solve it together but you're

judged alone

• Three difficulties — anomaly variety and the help in your hands

both change

• Hundreds of object variants, shifting lock layouts

────────────────────────────

SO — WHO IS WRONG?

Every room has a different rule. Observe your surroundings, coordinate with your team, and figure out what the giant buttons in front of you actually do.

Features

  • Hold, toggle, and other button behaviors

Always playing: your desktop is Widget Idle's controller!

Satisfying animations and gameplay!

We carefully designed every interaction you'll have in Widget Idle.

From big feature unlocks to the smallest page switch, we hope these animations and sounds are ones you'll never want to put down!

Ever-evolving desktop companions!

Explore hidden (and not-so-hidden) mechanics, and collect and curate 100+ unique achievement stamps. (Supports Steam's new achievement system at launch!)

Customize your experience!

You're free to adjust:

  • 7 accessible color palettes

  • Window zoom, with quick switching

Wishlist now!

Every 8 is wild

Wild Crazy 8s is a roguelike deckbuilder built on Crazy Eights — the card game where eights go wild. An 8 plays on anything, at any time, and lets you call the next suit. It rescues dead hands, keeps a scoring chain alive, and steers the pile toward the cards you're still holding. When to play your eights is the choice every run hinges on.

Chain cards, bank combos

On your turn, play any card that matches the pile's suit or rank — or drop an 8 if you're feeling wild. Chain as many cards together as you can; each one scores (base chips + card value) × Boost, and your Combo climbs with every card and carries over between turns. He was a straw man—a director in name only, whose name and signature kept the people actually in control off the paperwork.

A damaged recording on Marek’s answering machine gives him reason to doubt the official story.   • A cross-border investigation spanning real locations in Bratislava and Prague in 1993.
  • Documents, signatures, and contradictions that reward close attention.
  • Conversations that respond to what Marek has already uncovered.

The Wild is growing back: taller, thornier and full of monsters. Grab your scythe, gather your squad and push it back one swing at a time. Wild Heroes: Fight Together is a 1–4 player online co-op action roguelite where every expedition is a fight for the whole team.

Carve Into the Wild


Set out from your camp's Whetstone Shrine and cut your way outward. The deeper you go, the tougher and more toxic the Wild becomes, and the faster your blade dulls. Dig up buried gem hoards, upgrade your scythe and decide how far your squad dares to push.

Fight Together, Fall Together


When a wave hits, bramble walls rise around your group and nobody leaves until the arena is clear. Stick close for bigger fights, revive fallen friends mid-battle and guard your shared lives: lose them all and the expedition is over.

Three Acts, Three Titans


Each run is a long expedition across three acts. Break the charging Bramblehorn, outlast the spore-spewing Sporemother, then march into the lair of the Weedking for the final showdown.

Stronger Every Run


Draft perks from a three-card pick as you level up, bank Star Seeds when a boss falls, and spend them on new heroes, perks and relics you carry into your next run. Beat it all? Raise the Bramble Rank and go again.

Features

  • Play solo or in 1–4 player online co-op, with Steam invites, drop-in hot-join and proximity voice chat
  • 8 heroes across 4 classes (Harvester, Warden, Herbalist, Striker), each with a signature skill and an ultimate
  • A 24-wave expedition in three acts with three boss fights
  • Shared team lives, mid-fight revives and arenas that grow with your squad
  • 15 perks drafted from 3-card picks, plus unlockable relics
  • Meta progression: unlock heroes, perks and relics with Star Seeds
  • 10 Bramble Ranks for veterans and a Relaxed mode for a gentler run
  • Save mid-run and continue your expedition later

EVERY ERA IS A NEW WORLD

Up to 50 Spirits enter a newly generated world. Each Era lasts 28 minutes.

Explore, gather Vital Energy and materials, build defenses.

Form alliances or fight for the resources and protection you need.

When the Era ends, the world disappears.

Only Spirits protected by a RELIC endure.

EVERY SPIRIT BEGINS AS PURE

You don’t choose a class.

What you become depends on what you do within the world.

Your actions shape your form, your strengths and the way you interact with everything around you.

WHAT WILL YOU BECOME TO SURVIVE?

YOU ARE NOT ALONE

Some will help you survive.

Others will want what you have.

Meanwhile, the Era moves on.

The Void Spirits grow stronger.

THE JUDGMENT

Everything that happens during an Era leads to this moment.

When the final day comes, the world disappears.

Only the protection of a RELIC allows a Spirit to endure.

Those who survive add another Era to their history, growing wiser and stronger.

Wild Spirits Era is an independent passion project

Every wishlist, every bug report and every message helps this world continue to grow.

Developer: Nico — a Wild Spirit

From The Developer

I was a pilot in the 90s and flew out of an airport that was shared with a CAL FIRE air attack base. My memories of watching the bombers flying their missions inspired this game. The look and feel is inspired by my favorite early arcade vector games as well as the ATC equipment in use at the time.

You run the air attack. You guide the planes.

A wildfire is burning and the attack aircraft are yours to direct. You are the air attack supervisor, orbiting above with a radio and a map on a phosphor console. Air tankers, VLATs, and helitack crews check in and wait for your call. Your job is to read the situation, decide where retardant and water will do the most good, draw the lines, and live with how the fire answers.

One sitting, not a campaign

Most fires are decided in under half an hour, shorter if you accelerate time. The score at the end tells you how well you did: acres burned, structures lost, and whether you ever got a line around the fire. Try it again or save the replay to come back to later. Your high scores are saved per fire.

How It Plays

  • Drag on the map to lay a drop line. It anchors where you press and runs the way you drag.

  • Retardant holds ground. It does not put fire out, it makes fuel refuse to burn, so a line laid across the front buys you everything beyond it.

  • Water puts flames out on contact and then dries. Spend it on what is burning now.

  • Helitack dip from the nearest water, so how often they come back is determined by where water can be found (lakes and shorelines or the Air Attack Base).

  • Every airframe has a turnaround time: load, fly, drop, return. The queue is the real constraint, not the map.

  • Pause whenever you like, and compress time up to 16x while the fire is quiet.

The fire is a simulation, not a script

Fire spreads faster uphill and faster downwind, through fuel that changes across the map. Grass runs and burns out. Timber holds, then throws embers ahead of itself. Wind shifts, and the line you spent four loads on is suddenly the wrong one. Lightning ignites new starts while you are still working the first one. The fire you were sent to is not always the only fire you leave with.

Containment is measured honestly, as the share of the perimeter with nowhere left to burn, and acres burned is a count of what actually burned. The same fire fought differently becomes a different fire.

What's In It

  • Eleven authored fires. Six training fires, each built around an idea, and five drawn from real incidents: the Rim Fire, Horse River, the Marshall Fire, the Palisades Fire, and the Canberra fire, each with its own weather, fuel, and terrain.

  • Generated incidents, without end. Every one is rolled fresh and rated for difficulty before you commit to it, from a quiet ridge at dawn to a coastal town under a heavy offshore wind.

  • Two-player co-op. Two airbases, two rosters, and one mission. You see the other commander's aircraft and the lines they have drawn, and you command only your own. Practice with a bot.

  • A replay of every run, with a code you can hand to somebody else so they can watch and fly the exact fire you fought. The simulation is deterministic, so what they get is your fire, not just a recording of it.

  • High Score saved per fire.

  • 28 achievements, all earned by flying well rather than by flying often.

  • A recorded radio net. Your crews call in, read back and report, with voices that change from one mission to the next.

  • Nine tracks of music.

  • Plays on a controller or with mouse and keyboard, with on-screen control hints you can hide.

Survive the forest you awakened


A failed elixir has stirred something ancient beneath the roots. In Wildixir, a single-player fantasy survivor roguelite, you wield alchemy against the creatures of a corrupted wilderness. Your spells attack automatically; you choose where to move, when to dash, and which formulas will carry you through the next wave.

Two weapons. Unpredictable chemistry.


Pair magical weapons, develop their formulas and discover powerful evolutions. Combine frost with lightning, trigger an acid reaction in a poison pool, or hold your ground behind a ring of thorns. Build around the reactions you create and lead enemies into their path.

Heal the land — or make it dangerous


Cleansing a shrine gives you a choice: grow a healing grove, or cultivate a dangerous garden for greater rewards. Each decision changes how you use the battlefield. Will you create a refuge or risk another fight for a stronger build?

Three corrupted lands


Fight through an enchanted forest, a poisonous marsh and crystalline ruins. Each land brings its own hazards, enemy encounters and final boss. Learn their attacks and adapt your route as the pressure rises.

Bring something back from every attempt


Unlock distinct alchemists, new weapons and trials by completing journal objectives. Spend the seeds you earn on lasting upgrades, experiment with different schools of alchemy, and return with a new plan.

  • Automatic attacks, active movement and a dash to escape danger.
  • Three playable characters with distinct appearances and animations.
  • Eleven weapons, weapon evolutions and passive formulas to shape your build.
  • Three maps with different hazards and bosses.
  • Four unlockable trials for a different kind of challenge.
  • Journal objectives and permanent progression between runs.

She lives behind your windows

Not an overlay, and not always-on-top. She lives on the wallpaper layer, behind every window you have open, across all of your monitors at once. Close a window and you might catch her standing behind it. She has no window of her own; the desktop is her window.

She has opinions about you

Alt-click an empty patch of desktop and she'll come, usually at a lope, sometimes overshooting because she got a little too excited.

Or maybe she won't. Her refusals are never random; she always has a reason, and if you've been ignoring her, you're it.

Left alone, she doesn't just settle down. She escalates. First she looks up at where your cursor is. Then she drifts closer and stops just short. Then she starts inventing errands: rechecking a corner she already checked, acting like she meant to go there. If you still don't respond, she stops asking and puts her head down to graze, which is the only thing she does all day that isn't about you.

She sulks, too, when she's put herself out there for you, and you stop paying attention to her. If she crosses three monitors at a lope because you called and gets nothing for it, she'll turn her hindquarters to you and you'll have to earn her back.

After midnight she stops performing entirely and just stays close.

Things to do with a Wildmane horse

  • Hide carrots — four carrots appear on the desktop, tucked behind your open windows. Move a window, reveal a  carrot, and she'll spot it and run over. When she gets all four, she celebrates.

  • Play ball — click to send it rolling; she fetches and knocks it back with horse-grade aim. Ignore her for half a minute and she starts playing alone.

  • Tic-tac-toe — a board scratched into the ground. You place crossed sticks, she walks over and stomps a horseshoe. She's beatable. She's a horse. If she wins, she'll gloat.

  • Horseshoes — exactly what it sounds like.

Hand-built, one frame at a time

No motion capture, no asset store, no procedural gait solver. Twenty-two hand-animated clips by someone who's actually spent time around real horses: a proper walk, a real trot, a lope with the correct footfall order, a rear, two different bucks, and a graze where her head actually reaches the ground.

If her legs look right to you, that's why.

She knows she's a guest

She never steals a click: anything in a window belongs to that window. She runs at 30fps only while she can actually be seen; covered up or screen locked, she idles down to almost nothing. She doesn't read your keyboard, and nothing about you leaves your machine.

Assign her to individual monitors or set her paddock manually. Resize her, mute her, and pause her.

A herd

Wildmane horses are built to run alongside each other. This one is complete on her own; she is not a piece of a set, and nothing here will nag you to buy anything. But she was designed with company in mind.

Wildmark is a cozy idle RPG about a lone woodland Warden and the homestead they slowly bring back to life. Every corner of the wilds is an illustrated diorama: a woodcutter's glade, a lantern-lit mine, a fishing pool, a camp kitchen, a forge, an old fighting ring. Visit for five minutes or a whole evening. Your Warden keeps working while you're gone.




  • Gather: Woodcutting, Foraging, Hunting, Fishing and Mining, each with its own quiet rhythm. Trees shudder and fall, ore sparks, and the Warden really does the work.
  • Craft: fletch bows and arrows, smith weapons and armour at the anvil, cook over the campfire, brew blessings in the cauldron.
  • Defend: patrol the meadow, the dark firs and the ruined watchtower. Every skill you raise makes the Warden stronger.
  • Chart: Cartography surveys the land, finds its hidden places and sends your expeditions further.




Your homestead starts as a bare island in the clouds. Each lot you can build on shows its building as an ink sketch, and when you build it, colour floods in. The hut becomes a cabin, the cabin becomes a lodge, and the garden, the smokehouse, the apiary and the watchtower rise around it. Every building earns something while the game is closed, and hired apprentices gather for you around the clock.




The wilds change with the seasons, and so does the work. Spring brings showers and blossom, summer brings heat and thunderstorms, autumn brings gales and fog, and winter brings snow that settles on the ground. Lanterns glow brighter as the sky darkens, and you can hear it all: rain on the roof, wind in the pines, cicadas on hot afternoons, crickets at night.





The Wildmark is a world of islands above the clouds. Every region you reach is painted in on the Map; the rest wait under cloud as an ink sketch. Set out by expedition to chart the Ashen Reach, a burnt forest still warm under the ash, and the Stormcrown Isles, high above the storm. Each brings new work for every skill, new beasts and Trials, a new tier of gear, and a higher level cap, all the way to 75. And every region hides small places to find: an old Warden's cache, a drowned shrine, a page of lore.





Forge your first blade and the endless Arena opens: wave after wave of tougher foes, paying gold and Valor into a deep tree of permanent upgrades. And beyond the patrol roads wait the great beasts: Greywind the Alpha, Warlord Vane, Ironhide the Titan.




  • True offline progress: your current skill, your patrol, the homestead and the apprentices keep working while you're away. (Your Warden comes home to rest before a fight could go wrong, and trials wait for you.)
  • Companions and Bonds: a squirrel, a hound, an otter, a falcon, a raven and more. The longer you work together the closer you grow, and a close friend walks the trail with you into any skill.
  • Guilds and goals: a Guild Ledger for every skill with tasks and ranks, a Completion page for the whole Wildmark, and a Surveyor you can hire to explore while you work.
  • Places, not menus: the Warden stands in his quarters in what he wears, contracts hang on a real notice board, and you sell over the counter of a pedlar's cart.
  • Curios & relics: collect woodland trinkets and attune them for lasting power.
  • Pass the Torch: retire a Warden to earn Embers and permanent Legacy upgrades for the next.
  • No pressure: no energy meters, no timers you have to answer, no microtransactions.




You asked, we built. You told us Wildmark should keep working while you're away, so patrols now fight on while the game is closed. You asked to see what your Warden is doing from any screen, to stop a craft at the right moment, for goals beyond the next level, and for a way to tell us what you think. All of it is in the game now. Thank you for every note.

Steam Cloud keeps your Warden with you across devices, and Steam Achievements and a global Arena leaderboard mark the milestones.

Wander in. The forest remembers its Warden.

Wirehawk brings back the arcade shmup of the golden age, redrawn in glowing vector lines on pure black - with a choice of two control modes, each tuned for its device.

Mouse mode delivers modern, precise control - your ship goes exactly where your hand goes, fast and pixel-sharp. Controller mode is built for the stick: enemy fire, contact speeds and warnings are tuned so a gamepad plays fair, with its own progress and its own leaderboards.

You just fly; your laser never stops firing. Fight your way up through the stages of distinct neon worlds, face a boss every tenth stage, and push your laser from a single beam to a screen-filling fan of over twenty.

Score high enough and Nightmare unlocks: endless waves that get faster, denser and tougher, one life, no god mode, and a leaderboard of its own.

  • Pure neon vector look - every line drawn, no sprites

  • Asteroid runs, alien arenas, boss fights

  • Reaction over memorization - no scripted waves, each enemy hunts you with its own behavior

  • Power-ups, helper drones, homing missiles and time-slowing stasis

  • Two control modes - razor-sharp mouse or a controller mode tuned for the stick; autofire always on

  • Nightmare mode - endless waves, one life, unlocked by score, with its own leaderboards

  • Short runs, instant restarts, old-school "one more go" scoring

  • Global Steam leaderboards - separate boards for mouse and controller, every world you conquer counts

Overview

You begin as nothing — a mote of raw magic drifting through a world that doesn't know your name yet. Absorb elemental energy from the world around you,

transform your Wisp, and grow powerful enough to challenge a world boss. Then die, bank your Shards, and try again stronger.

WISP: Elemental Conflict is a top-down elemental roguelike where your build is made of the world itself.

---

Absorb. Shape. Survive.

Elemental motes scatter across every biome. Collect them. Pour them into your abilities to change how they behave — a Fire Dart ignites on contact, a

Void Nova shreds, a Crystal Shield erupts with shrapnel when it breaks. The same 11 abilities express themselves across 12 distinct elements: Fire,

Water, Ice, Lightning, Wind, Earth, Metal, Crystal, Wood, Light, Dark, and Void.

Invest motes into your three body stats — Vitality, Armor, and Mana — to shape who your Wisp becomes. Reallocate freely between runs. Experiment without

penalty.

---

A Living World at War With Itself

The ecosystem isn't waiting for you. It has its own agenda.

8 distinct creature types compete for resources and territory across every run — and most of them will turn on you the moment you step into their range:

- Sprites forage peacefully — until you're the most interesting thing nearby

- Hunters sprint and stalk with predatory aggression

- Lurkers stalk invisibly and pounce from the shadows

- Swarms coordinate in packs — disturb one, disturb all

- Sentinels guard their territory with ranged precision

- Wraiths fire from distance and retreat when pressed

- Colossi are armored tanks that charge and retaliate

- Harbingers dodge your shots, raise damage shields, and burst-fire in rings

---

4 Worlds. 12 Biomes. 12 Bosses.

Every run takes you through one of four worlds — The Burning Reaches, The Fractured Expanse, The Sunken Realm, or The Abyssal Hollow — each home to three

elementally themed biomes and a named world boss. The Emberlord. The Tide Sovereign. The Prism Oracle. The Ancient Still. Each boss is a signature

elemental encounter. Defeat one to end your run and claim your Shards.

Worlds unlock through meta-progression — each victory opens the door to harder terrain, stranger creatures, and more powerful rewards.

---

Grow Between Runs

Shards are the only currency that survives death. Spend them to expand your mote capacity, unlock new abilities, and push deeper into worlds that don't

pull their punches. Every run is a clean slate. Every run builds on everything that came before.

---

Key Features

- 12 elemental motes — each changes the behavior, visuals, and feel of every ability

- 11 abilities — Dart, Dash, Shield, Orb, Lance, Nova, Aura, Teleport, Vortex, Stealth, Seeker

- 3 body stats shaped by mote investment — Vitality, Armor, Mana

- 8 creature types in a living ecosystem with their own behaviors and rivalries

- 12 named elemental bosses, one per biome

- 4 worlds across 12 procedurally generated biomes

- Persistent meta-progression via Shards — grow permanently between runs

- Casual-friendly run length — pick up, play, and put down without losing your footing

"Witch Hunt 0" is a magic-focused, stage-based boss rush 3D action game.

Take on the role of the witch Astera. To reclaim her lost powers, she must craft spells, tame defeated enemies as familiars, and conquer the formidable foes that stand in her way.

■Intense Battles Between Witches

To make our rival witches think and act more like humans, we’ve incorporated a "prediction" mechanic into some of their spells.

They will anticipate your movements and attack accordingly, making your positioning and decision-making more crucial than ever.

Furthermore, the game's signature "Ultimate Spells" require incantation time—and since your enemies can cast them too, you’ll experience intense, high-stakes magical clashes.

■ Build Your Magic, Create the Ultimate Strategy

By crafting a wide variety of spells, you can pursue a combat style that suits you best.

Spells are divided into eight elements—Fire, Water, Ice, Wind, Thunder, Earth, Light, and Dark—each with its own unique status effects.

■ Tame Enemies and Hunt Together

To collect Minions, you must challenge the "Binary Trials," a Roguelite dungeon where the monsters change with every run.

As you ascend through the layers, you’ll have a higher chance of recruiting powerful Minions, but the strength of the monsters will skyrocket alongside your progress.

Overlap patterns. Build powerful combos.

Arrange cards on a 3×3 grid to form spell patterns, from straights and flushes to familiar symbols. Use the same cards in multiple patterns to build bigger combos and generate more mana. Find the strongest combination in the cards you're dealt.

Shape your strategy with items and enchantments

Learn new patterns and choose which ones to upgrade. Spend Mana Stones on items, then combine their effects with card enchantments to boost your mana and combos. Browse the layouts in your Spellbook to plan your next move.

Explore Oz with the magic you create

Explore lakeshores, rye fields, and forests with Dorothy, and meet the Tin Man, Scarecrow, and Lion along the way. Turn your cards into lightning, grass, and fire to help your companions. Hidden markings hold clues to new magic.

Playable in English and Korean.

Stop the Curse, Save the town!

Your Witch master’s dying action was to curse the town. Now supernatural thorns are spreading across the town, and you may be the only person capable of stopping them.

Investigate the town, build relationships, follow rumors, earn money, uncover hidden places, and discover the ingredients needed to complete a ritual before the curse consumes everything.

But every run is different. You won’t need the same ingredients every time, not everyone will willingly help you, and saving the town may require deciding what kind of witch you are willing to become.

100 Days to Break a Curse

The thorns spread every day. You have limited actions to spend each day, forcing you to decide what matters most: investigating a lead, earning money, strengthening a relationship, gathering supplies, or trying to push the curse back.

Waste too much time and the town can be lost.

Investigate a Town Full of Secrets

Explore the town and its surroundings, follow rumors, uncover hidden routes, investigate strange events, and piece together what people know about the curse.

From the Chapel and crowded Inn to forgotten Underground Passages, Plague Pits, ancient Ritual Circles, and the edge of the evil Thornwood, Different locations will reveal different pieces of the mystery and why everything happened the way it did.

Decide Who to Trust

The people of the town have their own problems, loyalties, secrets, and opinions of you.

Build relationships through conversation, favors, gifts, and difficult choices. People who trust you may provide information, resources, access to places you could not otherwise reach, or even agree to help you complete the ritual.

Discover the Ritual You Need

There are ten possible ritual ingredients, but only five are required in each run to win.

Learn what you need, discover where those ingredients can be found, and work out how to obtain them. Some require exploration. Others depend on relationships, favors,  or secrets.

Finding all 10 ingredients  may reveal possibilities beyond merely surviving the curse.

Manage Cutting back Thorns and Earning Money

The thorns are growing quickly and will need to be cut back. You must balance rituals, aid from townsfolk and your own efforts to keep them in check or risk the town being overrun by thorns before 100 days have passed.

Choose What Kind of Witch You Become

Be good and honest or manipulative and sneaky, your actions and decisions will shape the ending of your story.  Compromise your morals for quick success or find ethical ways to get access.

Built for Replayability with Achievement and Secrets

Different required ingredients, discoveries, random events, outfits, achievements, and multiple endings mean that a new apprentice does not have to follow the same path as the last.

Hidden locations and NPCs

Of course, a town of secrets has hidden places to explore and NPCs to find. Discover the truth of the sewers and other mysteries!

WizKitty and the Tower of Doom, Gloom, and Other Bad Stuff is a roguelike deckbuilder where your deck doesn’t fight, it crafts the weapon that does.

Every run is a puzzle of modifiers, upgrades, rerolls, prefixes, suffixes, and trying to bully RNG into giving you the perfect item.

Build a ridiculous weapon. Smash your way up the tower. Laugh in the face of RNG.

Inspired by the strategic decision-making of Slay the Spire, the escalating “one more run” energy of Balatro, and the item-crafting obsession of Path of Exile, WizKitty is built for players who love broken builds, surprising synergies, and losing sleep to one more run.

Features

  • Deckbuilding meets weapon crafting

    • Use your cards to add, remove, upgrade, reroll, and transform weapon modifiers.

  • Every weapon tells a story

    • Turn a sad little stick into a blazing, overpowered mistake that somehow works.

  • Chase broken builds

    • Stack synergies, exploit weird interactions, and push your weapon far past reasonable behavior.

  • Climb the Tower of Doom, Gloom, and Other Bad Stuff

    • Face enemies, unlock new possibilities, and discover increasingly strategic ways to win.

  • A tiny wizard cat with very big ambitions

    • WizKitty may be small, but the weapons are not.
